samples.summary: No test that a real `table` block survives the new clipboard sanitizer — only the negative "dropped" case is covered
samples.evidence: The change replaces `payload.blocks as Block[]` with a full rebuild, so every copied `table` block must now pass `sanitizeTableData` (clipboard.ts:255-274), which rebuilds `rows/columnWidths/rowHeights` and returns `undefined` on any shape mismatch — in which case `sanitizeBlock` returns null and the block is silently DROPPED from the paste (clipboard.ts:292-297). `text-editor.ts:1092` copies selected blocks (tables included) through `serializeClipboard`. The only new table assertion is the negative one: `deserializeBlocks(JSON.stringify({version:1, blocks:[{type:'table'}]}))).toEqual([])` (clipboard.test.ts:246). Nothing round-trips a serialized table block and asserts rows/cell text/columnWidths survive, so a sanitizer that drops or mangles every pasted table would keep the suite green. Searched: `deserializeBlocks|deserializeClipboard|WAFFLEDOCS_MIME` across packages/docs/test (only clipboard.test.ts and list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts, neither serializes a table block), plus test/model/paste-table-into-cell.test.ts and test/model/nested-table.test.ts do not touch the clipboard JSON path.

samples.summary: `sanitizeImageData` is new required-path code for every copied inline image, with no test
samples.evidence: Pasted inline images now only survive if `sanitizeImageData` (clipboard.ts:110-128) recovers them; it returns `undefined` unless `src`, `width` and `height` are all present, and rebuilds `alt`/`rotation`/crop/`originalWidth`/`originalHeight` key by key. No test in the new `clipboard payload validation` block (clipboard.test.ts:177-259) nor in the pre-existing round-trip tests supplies an inline with `style.image`, so copy/paste silently stripping images (or dropping crops/rotation) would not fail any lane. Searched clipboard.test.ts for `image`/`src` (absent) and grepped the docs test dir for clipboard deserialization callers.

`asStoredColor` (clipboard.ts:90-108) handles three shapes; the only colour assertions in the suite use the legacy string form (`color: '#ff0000'`, clipboard.test.ts:143). A regression that dropped role-based (theme) colours on paste — the common case for themed docs — would pass. No new test exercises `{kind:'role', role:'accent1', tint:0.4}`.

samples.summary: Cell-level sanitization details untested: colSpan/rowSpan, borders, verticalAlign, empty-blocks fallback
samples.evidence: `sanitizeCell`/`sanitizeCellStyle`/`sanitizeBorder` (clipboard.ts:205-243) newly gate merged-cell spans (`colSpan > 1` truncation), the four border objects and `verticalAlign`. The one new tableCells test (clipboard.test.ts:249-258) only asserts a bad `headingLevel` and a bad `padding`. Copy/paste of merged cells or bordered cells losing those attrs would not be caught.
searchedFor: read clipboard.test.ts 'validates the tableCells half' test

samples.summary: `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH` nesting cap has no test, though the code comment presents it as the guard against unbounded nesting
samples.evidence: clipboard.ts:59 documents the cap and clipboard.ts:256 enforces `depth >= MAX_TABLE_DEPTH`, but no test constructs a nested-table payload deeper than the limit to assert the inner table is dropped rather than recursed into. `MAX_LIST_LEVEL` got a test (clipboard.test.ts:236-239); the depth cap did not.

samples.summary: Block-id regeneration is an explicit new behavior (`id: generateBlockId()`) with no assertion
samples.evidence: clipboard.ts:283-286 states ids are regenerated so a payload cannot collide with a live block id — a stated security property. No test asserts `deserializeBlocks` returns an id different from the payload's (`parseOne` in clipboard.test.ts:178 never inspects `id`; the pre-existing round-trip tests pass `id:'b1'` but only assert inlines/type). Restoring `id: record.id` would keep the suite green.

clipboard.ts:193-203 rebuilds `block.marker` for list items and returns `undefined` when empty. No test in the new validation block copies a list item with a custom marker, so silently dropping marker formatting on paste would not fail.

samples.summary: The exported predicates `splitMovesHeadingMemory`/`mergeDropsHeadingMemory` have no direct unit tests; one clause is only reachable there
samples.evidence: Both are newly exported from block-helpers.ts (290, 315) and consumed by two implementations (applySplitBlock and YorkieDocStore). Coverage is only indirect via Doc/editor/yorkie tests; `packages/docs/test/store/block-helpers.test.ts` was not touched (grep for the names shows no test file hit besides list-heading-roundtrip's use of `unlistedBlockType`). In particular the `block.inlines.some(text.length > 0)` clause (offset-0 split of an *empty* bulleted list item) is unreachable through `Doc.splitBlock`, which short-circuits empty list items, so nothing exercises it.
searchedFor: grep splitMovesHeadingMemory|mergeDropsHeadingMemory across repo — only src, yorkie-doc-store, docs/design; no test file asserts on them directly

samples.summary: The entry-parity test asserts on regex-scraped source text, not on real importability, so it can pass while the exports are broken
samples.evidence: `blockHelperExports` (entry-parity.test.ts:18-30) reads index.ts/node.ts as strings and matches only `export { … } from '…'` with single quotes and the exact literal `./store/block-helpers.js`. A name mistyped in BOTH entries, or a helper re-exported via `export * from` / double quotes / a re-export chain, satisfies the assertion. It never imports either entry to confirm the symbol resolves — which is the failure mode the file comment says it guards ('fails at import time there'). A dynamic `await import('../../src/node.js')` symbol check would test the stated behavior.
searchedFor: checked src/index.ts and src/node.ts export forms in the diff

samples.summary: The `pastedTextLen > 0` guard on the single-block paste memory drop is untested
samples.evidence: text-editor.ts:3596 only drops the remembered level when the pasted text is non-empty. The paste tests in list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts cover the non-empty case ('text pasted into an emptied bulleted heading drops the memory', line ~530) but never paste an empty-text single block into an empty bulleted heading to assert the memory is KEPT, so removing the `pastedTextLen > 0` guard would not fail anything.

samples.summary: Heading-level coercion tests skip the non-numeric-to-NaN and 0 fallbacks
samples.evidence: `Math.trunc(Number(headingLevel)) || 1` also has to handle `undefined`/`null`/`{}` (NaN → 1) and `0` → 1; the new tests cover a quote-breaking string, 42, 2.7 and -3 only (docx-style-map.test.ts:99-115). Low impact since the clamp is exercised, but the NaN branch is the one an attacker-supplied object hits.

finding.summary: No test that a real `table` block survives the new clipboard sanitizer — only the negative "dropped" case is covered
finding.evidence: The change replaces `payload.blocks as Block[]` with a full rebuild, so every copied `table` block must now pass `sanitizeTableData` (clipboard.ts:255-274), which rebuilds `rows/columnWidths/rowHeights` and returns `undefined` on any shape mismatch — in which case `sanitizeBlock` returns null and the block is silently DROPPED from the paste (clipboard.ts:292-297). `text-editor.ts:1092` copies selected blocks (tables included) through `serializeClipboard`. The only new table assertion is the negative one: `deserializeBlocks(JSON.stringify({version:1, blocks:[{type:'table'}]}))).toEqual([])` (clipboard.test.ts:246). Nothing round-trips a serialized table block and asserts rows/cell text/columnWidths survive, so a sanitizer that drops or mangles every pasted table would keep the suite green. Searched: `deserializeBlocks|deserializeClipboard|WAFFLEDOCS_MIME` across packages/docs/test (only clipboard.test.ts and list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts, neither serializes a table block), plus test/model/paste-table-into-cell.test.ts and test/model/nested-table.test.ts do not touch the clipboard JSON path.

verdict.reason: The new sanitizer path for `table` blocks is real and reachable: `sanitizeTableData` (clipboard.ts:255-274) can return undefined, in which case `sanitizeBlock` returns null and `sanitizeBlocks` silently drops the table block (clipboard.ts:292-298, 324-332); copy/cut of block selections (text-editor.ts:1091-1093, 1120-1122) and paste (text-editor.ts:1240-1242) exercise exactly that path. I could find no positive test that a serialized table block survives it. In clipboard.test.ts the only table payload sent through deserializeBlocks is the negative drop case (line 246); every other `type === 'table'` assertion (lines 494-539, 611-689) exercises parseHtmlToBlocks/parseMarkdownWithTables, which construct tables via createTableBlock and never touch sanitizeTableData. The positive tableCells round-trip (lines 89-120) covers sanitizeCellRows/sanitizeCell, not the rows/columnWidths/rowHeights rebuild. Repo-wide greps for deserializeBlocks|deserializeClipboard|serializeClipboard|serializeBlocks|WAFFLEDOCS_MIME|x-waffledocs and for `version: 1, blocks` surface only clipboard.test.ts and list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts; I read the latter in full and its pasteBlocks helper (lines 454-472) only ever passes paragraph/heading/list-item blocks. Other clipboard-event tests (editor-read-only.test.ts:229-248, link-trailing-edge.test.ts:125) do not round-trip a table via the JSON path, there are no docs e2e/.spec suites, and no in-src vitest suites for packages/docs. A sanitizer that dropped or mangled every pasted table would keep the suite green, so this is a behavior change with no meaningful positive coverage.

finding.summary: `sanitizeImageData` is new required-path code for every copied inline image, with no test
finding.evidence: Pasted inline images now only survive if `sanitizeImageData` (clipboard.ts:110-128) recovers them; it returns `undefined` unless `src`, `width` and `height` are all present, and rebuilds `alt`/`rotation`/crop/`originalWidth`/`originalHeight` key by key. No test in the new `clipboard payload validation` block (clipboard.test.ts:177-259) nor in the pre-existing round-trip tests supplies an inline with `style.image`, so copy/paste silently stripping images (or dropping crops/rotation) would not fail any lane. Searched clipboard.test.ts for `image`/`src` (absent) and grepped the docs test dir for clipboard deserialization callers.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. sanitizeImageData (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:110-128) is on the mandatory paste path for every inline image (sanitizeInlineStyle line 160-161 -> sanitizeInlines -> sanitizeBlock -> sanitizeBlocks, the only path used by deserializeBlocks:22 and deserializeClipboard:347, which text-editor.ts:1240 invokes for every WAFFLEDOCS_MIME paste). I enumerated ALL callers of serializeBlocks/deserializeBlocks/serializeClipboard/deserializeClipboard repo-wide: only two test files (clipboard.test.ts, list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts), and neither contains any `image`/`src:` fixture. The style round-trip test (clipboard.test.ts:130-167) covers bold/italic/superscript/href/fontSize/colors but no image; the validation block (177-259) covers headingLevel, block type, unknown keys, listLevel, broken payloads and tableCells, but no image case. I also grepped all test files for `version: 1` payloads (only clipboard.test.ts), listed every packages/docs test file (the ones using style.image are renderer/export/import tests that never touch clipboard serialization), and confirmed no e2e suite exists. Therefore a regression in which pasted images are stripped entirely or lose crop/rotation/originalWidth/originalHeight would fail no test — required-path behavior with no meaningful coverage, major under the test-adequacy rubric.

finding.summary: The text-box editor's `toggleList` exit change ships with no behavioral test
finding.evidence: The diff changes three parallel `toggleList` implementations to exit through `unlistedBlockType`: `view/editor.ts` (covered by `list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts` → 'toggleList round trip'), `view/text-editor.ts` (covered by 'keyboard bullet shortcut round trip'), and `view/text-box-editor.ts:1125` — which has no coverage. The only existing test touching it is `packages/docs/test/view/text-box-editor.test.ts:327` ('exposes toggleList, indent, outdent'), which asserts `typeof api.toggleList === 'function'` and `expect(() => api.toggleList('unordered')).not.toThrow()` on a paragraph with no selection — it passes identically whether the exit produces a heading or a paragraph, so it is fake coverage for this change. Ironically the new test file's own comment says both toggleList paths 'must exit through unlistedBlockType or the keyboard path silently drifts', yet only two of the three named implementations are exercised.

verdict.reason: The text-box editor's toggleList exit IS covered by a dedicated behavioral test suite. packages/docs/test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:598-663 ('text-box editor toggleList round trip') imports the real initializeTextBox from ../../src/view/text-box-editor.js (line 7), mounts it on a real container+canvas (lines 614-628), and asserts the round trip: bullet a Heading 2 then check list-item with headingLevel 2, un-bullet then check {type:'heading', headingLevel:2} (lines 630-639); a paragraph stays a paragraph with headingLevel undefined (641-651); switching bullet kind still restores Heading 3 (653-662). Those assertions read the live block via getBlockType() (src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1093-1102) and would fail if the exit at src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1121-1137 hardcoded 'paragraph' instead of unlistedBlockType(block). The suite's own header comment (lines 598-603) explicitly names initializeTextBox as 'the third toggleList implementation', directly contradicting the finding's claim that only two of the three are exercised. The reviewer searched test/view/text-box-editor.test.ts; the real coverage lives in list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts next to the other two paths.
